title: 113mph Truck Pursuit Ends in Total Disaster
description:
Why so many PITs? With some vehicles, active stability control can help a driver recover from an otherwise successful PIT. Not the first time we've seen it happen: https://youtu.be/cm3mx_uEWTY?si=Mv60cfqt6zGenclp

Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

The suspect, identified at the scene as Russell Kane-Cornigay, was taken to Marion County Jail and charged with possession of methamphetamine, possession of drug paraphernalia, possession of cannabis, Possession of cannabis less than 20 grams, felony fleeing police with disregard to safety, grand theft of a motor vehicle, resisting an officer without violence, false imprisonment, and driving with a suspended license. Originally, Russell entered a not-guilty plea. However, after almost eight months sitting in jail, he entered a plea deal. All of the drug charges, as well as the grand theft of a motor vehicle and the false imprisonment charges were dropped. In exchange, Russell pleaded guilty to the remaining charges and was sentenced to time served just a week shy of eight months. He was also assessed fines and court costs of over $54,000 and has agreed to pay $50 a month. At that rate, it will take Russell 90 years to square up with the state of Florida.
